title: Cedar-compatible serialization of the authorization registry
summary: Fix a canonical policy document for the unified authorization registry: normalized request (principal/action/resource/context), 3-value decision contract, and valid-Cedar rendering. Key lessons: the registry data plane is FLAT (overlay+plugin one tier; precedence = code>data, exact>prefix, longest prefix, provider order); Cedar >= is long-only, in is entity-membership-only, Action:: has no glob, and Cedar has no catch-all — prefix denies must be forbid-when{subject-match && !(conds)} and fail-safe defaults gate on context.declared == false. requires_lineage is a declaration attribute (delegable), not a granted_when condition.
hint_triggers: P4 fixed the serialized authorization contract: SerializedAuthorizationDocument{version:1, defaults per axis, policies} enumerates every declaration of all four subject axes (operation/intent/capability/verb) and all layers with precedence provenance. The pure evaluator evaluatePolicyDocument must reproduce registry precedence exactly — the data plane is flat: [code?0:1, exact?0:1, -subject.length, overlay_index]. Cedar renderer emits valid Cedar only: numeric context.assurance_level (>= is long-only), || for task/tenant binding (in is entity-membership-only), context.action_subject like p:* for prefix subjects (Action ids have no glob), forbid when{subject-match && !(conds)} for unmet prefix policies and forbid unless{conds} for exact, defaults gated on context.declared == false (no catch-all exists). requires_lineage iff delegable — a declaration attribute, not a granted_when member. Meaning preservation is mechanically gated by comparing the document evaluator to live subjectAuthorization across a probe matrix incl. a synthetic overlay+plugin flat-data-layer fixture.
